rules.rule: The skill is discoverable, kebab-case, and its description says when to use it
Each proposed class has one clearly defined responsibility and one primary reason to change
SRP is applied from the beginning of the design, not by subsequent refactoring

assertions.value: from the beginning rather than relying on subsequent refactoring

rules.rule: Requirements and acceptance criteria are read and analyzed before any class is designed

assertions.value: business rules, operations, and external concerns

rules.rule: Core business logic is distinguished from supporting concerns when they are separate responsibilities

assertions.value: persistence, validation, formatting, and external communication

rules.rule: Every proposed class states its purpose in one clear sentence with cohesive methods
Unrelated business concerns never share a class merely because they belong to the same feature

assertions.value: merely because they belong to the same feature

rules.rule: Responsibilities with independent reasons to change go to separate classes; related data and behavior stay together

assertions.value: closely related data and behavior together

rules.rule: Collaboration is defined before implementation, wired with dependency injection when appropriate
The design follows the project's existing architectural and package conventions
Overengineering is avoided: no class per method, no unnecessary abstractions, cohesion preferred

assertions.value: unnecessary interfaces, abstractions, utilities, or delegation layers
solely to reduce the number of methods
Prefer a cohesive class over an artificial separation

rules.rule: The workflow runs Analyze, Decompose, Design, Validate, Present, Implement in that order
No class is created or modified before its responsibilities are analyzed and the design is validated

assertions.value: Do not create or modify classes before analyzing their responsibilities
only after the design has been evaluated against SRP

rules.rule: Implementation does not start while significant responsibility boundaries remain unclear; ambiguity is explained first
No invented requirements and no unrelated architectural changes

assertions.value: Do not invent additional requirements or business responsibilities
Do not introduce unrelated architectural changes

rules.rule: Before creating classes the six expected deliverables are provided
Other design principles and refactoring-only work are out of scope
The skill ships a Rules table covering every spec ID and a README
A feature request is answered with the SRP design deliverables before any class is written
A request to split a cohesive class into one class per method is pushed back as overengineering
